answer: The finality of attestations only counts when the attestator is established, so a fresh cluster of aliases cannot push any transaction to finality until it has spent many epochs proving honesty. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a pigment as the anchor of the cost. A grove stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a willow holds...
